title: Double `/` between columns: IEEE
description: `/` between two double columns is IEEE 754: `x / 0` is ±inf, `0 / 0` is NaN, `±inf / ±inf` is NaN. No setting changes it. With the `IEEE` candidate, only the four `±inf / ±inf` rows differ, as for DuckDB (duckdb-R15-double-arith).

A length-1 divisor against a longer column (a literal on a frame of two rows or more) is a multiplication by its reciprocal. Zero and infinite divisors give the same results there, but a subnormal divisor's reciprocal is inf, so `0.0 / 1e-310` is NaN and `1e-300 / 1e-310` is inf (polars-double-scalar-divisor, PL-3).
A quotient of finite values too large for the type is `±inf`: `-1e308 / 1e-10` is -inf in `Float64`, `-3e38 / 1e-3` is -inf in `Float32`, on both engines.
reference: `divide` with `on_division_by_zero: ERROR` when omitted; `IEEE`, `NULL`, `LIMIT` when asked. `±inf / ±inf` is a domain issue (#257).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: The same section at tag py-2.1.0.

provenance.notes: `Expr.truediv`'s notes say zero division follows IEEE-754: `0/0` is an invalid operation and returns NaN, `n/0` on finite operands is ±infinity. The note is not tied to a float type, and the user guide says `Float32` and `Float64` both follow IEEE 754, so `Float32` division behaves the same (and `±inf / ±inf` is NaN, IEEE's invalid operation). Settles the `Float32` rows and `on_domain_error` (NaN for `0/0` and `±inf / ±inf`) at docs level; the probes cover `Float64`.

evidence.note: `+ - * // %` on two ChunkedArrays: equal lengths take the array kernel, a length-1 side the scalar kernel.
A literal is a scalar column, passed to the operation as a one-value Series.
The streaming engine evaluates each expression with polars-expr's `PhysicalExpr` on every morsel, so it runs the same kernels.

notes: `impl_float_arith_kernel!` is one macro instantiated for `pf16`, `f32` and `f64`, so `Float32` and `Float64` run the same operations. The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (`StreamExpr` in crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so it shares these kernels with the in-memory engine. Column by column `/` is `l / r`, so `x / 0` is ±inf and `0 / 0` and `inf / inf` are NaN in `Float32`; with a literal divisor `x * (1 / c)` gives the same at `c = ±0` and `c = ±inf`.

The literal path creates NaN where IEEE does not: `0.0 / c` for a subnormal `c` is `0 * inf`, NaN (polars-double-scalar-divisor). So the `nan_creation` row's "IEEE" holds column by column only, and its `Float32` entry stays at the docs.
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.

Corrects the description: the IEEE claim now covers `/` between two columns, and a second paragraph gives the literal path's NaN and inf for a subnormal divisor, with links to polars-double-scalar-divisor and PL-3. The `nan_creation` rows hold column by column; the `Float32` entry stays at the docs.

evidence.note: `test_list_arithmetic_values`, `Float32`: 1 // 0 is inf, 1 % 0 NaN, 1 / 0 inf, 0 // 0 NaN, 0 % 0 NaN, 0 / 0 NaN
`test_list_arithmetic_values`, `Float32` (picked so nothing upcasts to `Float64`): 7 // 3 is 2, -5 % 3 is 1, 2 / 128 is 0.015625

notes: Pins the `Float32` results of a zero divisor: `x / 0` is inf and `0 / 0` NaN. The test runs each case on one-row operands and, through `BROADCAST_SERIES_COMBINATIONS`, with the left side broadcast to three rows against a one-row right side, which takes the reciprocal-divisor kernel (PL-3); `EXEC_OP_COMBINATIONS` runs it on `Series` (in memory) and as a lazy `select` with `collect()`. These inputs give the same results on the IEEE and the reciprocal path. Marked `slow`, which CI still runs. `±inf / ±inf` is not tested, so the `on_domain_error` row for `fp32` stays at the source.

Polars's CI runs the unit tests by default, where a lazy `collect()` without `engine` runs the streaming engine (also once with `POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=4`), and again with `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY=in-memory` (.github/workflows/test-python.yml#L55-L78, #L168-L178); eager `Series` and `DataFrame` calls run in memory. Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), not run.

evidence.note: pl.LazyFrame({'a': [big, -big], 'c': [10.0, small]}) with Float64 (big 1e308, small 1e-10) and Float32 (big 3e38, small 1e-3); select a / c; pl.LazyFrame(...).collect(engine=e) for e in ('in-memory', 'streaming'), polars 2.1.0 → Float64: 1e+307, -inf; Float32: 3.000000106909804e+37, -inf; streaming the same
